title: Perfect constant models for stratified finite-field etale complexes
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $k$ be a finite field. Let $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},k)$ be a bounded complex in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaf $k_X$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose every cohomology sheaf is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. There is a finite stratification of $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset] such that on an etale covering of each stratum $S$, $L|_S$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf complex of a bounded complex of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces; in particular the constant complex is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. After pro-etale comparison these are also the models of $(\nu_X^*L)|_S$, using [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. No integral lifting or completeness hypothesis is involved.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, forward implication, residue stratification; Proposition 6.8.11(3)

proof.text: Choose integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(L)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. For each of the finitely many integers $q$ in this interval, constructibility supplies a finite stratification with constructible locally closed strata on which $H^q(L)$ is finite locally constant as a sheaf of $k$-modules. Repeatedly apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection] to these stratifications. This gives one finite stratification $(i_s:S_s\to X)_s$ refining them all, with constructible images. The refinement uses the actual fibre-product schemes, not an unsupported factorization through a stratum based only on its underlying image. The one-factor starting case is the chosen stratification for $q=a$; at each subsequent integer intersect with the next chosen stratification. Empty fibre-product strata may be retained, since their images are disjoint and empty.

Fix a resulting stratum $i:S\to X$. Exactness of etale constant-ring module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $H^q(i^{-1}L)$ with $i^{-1}H^q(L)$: apply it to the kernels, images and quotients defining cohomology. Thus the same bounds $[a,b]$ hold. For each $q$ in this interval the refinement has a projection $p:S\to Z$ to the original stratum for $H^q(L)$. Pull back its trivializing etale covering $\{V_j\to Z\}$ to $\{S\times_Z V_j\to S\}$. On each member, pullback of the trivialized module is still the constant module with the same value, by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]. Therefore $H^q(i^{-1}L)$ is locally constant with finite module models. This also holds on every etale object $W\to S$, by base-changing the same covering to $W$. The zero cohomology sheaves outside $[a,b]$ have the constant zero model.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf); exact fixed-ring inverse image as in sites-modules.tex Tag 04JC

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-bounded-constant-models] to the scheme $S$, the finite commutative ring $B=k$ and $K=i^{-1}L$. Step 2 verifies both the uniform cohomology bounds and the local finite-generation hypothesis on every etale object. Obtain a jointly surjective etale covering $\{v_j:U_j\to S\}$ and, for each $j$, an isomorphism $v_j^{-1}i^{-1}L\simeq\underline{P_j^\bullet}_{\mathrm{et}}$. Here $P_j^\bullet$ is an actual complex of finite $k$-modules with terms zero outside $[a,b]$, and its sheaf differentials are induced by its module differentials. Every finite $k$-module is finite-dimensional: the finite list of all its elements spans it as a vector space. Hence these are the bounded finite-dimensional constant complex models asserted in the item.

source.place: Tag 094G, lemma-locally-constant, strengthened bounded constant-model assertion in the proof

proof.text: Each term $P_j^q$ is projective over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective], and it is finitely generated by step 3. Since $P_j^q=0$ outside $[a,b]$, $P_j^\bullet$ is already a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $k$-modules. Its derived object is therefore perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. The zero complex and zero terms satisfy the same criterion; no integral coefficient ring, lifting, or completeness enters this argument.

proof.text:
Let $h_j=i\circ v_j:U_j	o X$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to $i$ and $v_j$ to identify restriction of $
u_X^*L$ to $U_{j,\mathrm{proet}}$ with $
u_{U_j}^*(v_j^{-1}i^{-1}L)$. These comparisons apply termwise and descend to derived categories because the fixed-ring inverse images are exact [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. The functor $
u^*$ in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] is precisely that termwise module inverse image. In its finite commutative coefficient convention the pro-etale coefficient ring is identified with the constant ring sheaf, preserving constant sections, as stated in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Thus all these comparisons have the coefficient ring required by the item.

proof.text:
Apply $
u_{U_j}^*$ to the isomorphism from step 3. By [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module], naturally in every $k$-linear map, $
u_{U_j}^*\underline{P_j^q}_{\mathrm{et}}\cong\underline{P_j^q}_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Naturality for $d^q:P_j^q	o P_j^{q+1}$ gives commuting squares with the two constant differentials, so these isomorphisms form an isomorphism of complexes, not just of graded sheaves. In conjunction with step 5 this gives $(
u_X^*L)|_{U_j}\simeq\underline{P_j^ ullet}_{\mathrm{proet}}$ with exactly the perfect models of step 4. An etale covering is also a pro-etale covering by [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover], so it gives the asserted local models on every stratum. On the empty scheme the assertion is vacuous; empty strata require no nonzero model.

tool_uses.why: Generic change-of-topology covering lemma, used only to regard the resulting etale trivializations as pro-etale covers; it does not replace any unit proof step.

Generic natural constant-module comparison for geometric morphisms; used for refinement pullbacks and the site comparison. The unit has no equally general statement including naturality in module maps.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-ecc738d39 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 15 cited node statements, the parent integral-stratified characterization, the unit sk-thm-properbasechange, Stacks 094G (statement and full induction proof) and Bhatt–Scholze Prop. 6.6.11 (forward direction) and 6.8.11(3). The delivery is a first split with no new nodes, the statement is unchanged, review_split passes on the snapshot, and no SGA source is cited. Steps: (1) bounded interval, one constructibility stratification per degree, then repeated lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection, which uses real fibre-product schemes and constructible intersections. (2) Exactness from prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact(3) gives H^q(i^{-1}L)=i^{-1}H^q(L). The étale trivializing covers are pulled back along the refinement projections, and lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module keeps them constant with finite values on every étale W→S. (3) lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-bounded-constant-models (B=k finite commutative, a≤b) gives actual constant complexes of finite modules; Stacks 094G builds constant differentials. (4) Each term is projective by the Mathlib leaf and the complex is bounded, so it is perfect by def-pc-perfect-ring-complex; no claim is made over Z/4. (5) lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback, made termwise and derived by lem-pe exactness; the coefficient ring Cont(π0,Λ)^# is identified with the constant ring by prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, so the coefficient category does not change silently. (6) Naturality in lem-sfb gives an isomorphism of complexes, and étale covers are pro-étale covers (098B leaf). Edge cases checked: empty X and empty strata, L=0, a=b, the residue characteristic of X equal to char k, and non-split extensions. The statement is true and needs no ℓ-invertibility. Accepted tool uses: lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module and lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image, both generic topos facts used only for coefficients. The lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover declaration is redundant because that node is a Mathlib leaf. Duplicate search: lem-fin-lisse-field-site-perfect (F_ℓ only, no stratification), lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-derived-local-constancy (local-constancy ingredient only) and lem-sf-etale-smooth-stratified-ctf (different hypotheses) are not duplicates. No fixes.
